prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There’s no single universally “best” roofing company — the right one depends on your exact location in Miami, roof type, budget, and whether you need a full hurricane-rated upgrade vs. like-for-like replacement. I can find and vet top local contractors for you if you tell me your zip code or neighborhood. Meanwhile, use the checklist and tips below to identify a high-quality hurricane-rated roofer.

What to look for (must-haves)
- Florida roofing contractor license (look up on Florida DBPR; license type RC/Certified as required).
- Experience with Miami-Dade County/Florida product approvals and high-velocity hurricane zone (HVHZ) installations.
- Manufacturer certifications (e.g., GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, Owens Corning Preferred) — needed for enhanced warranties.
- Use of Miami‑Dade NOA-approved products and tested attachment methods (strapping, ring-shank nails, adhesives, proper underlayment).
- Proof of liability insurance and workers’ comp. Get the policy numbers and verify with insurer.
- Written permit handling and proper final inspection paperwork.
- Strong local references and recent projects in Miami, not just neighboring counties.
- Clear written contract: scope, products, manufacturer & contractor warranties, payment schedule, change order process.

Good-to-have
- Fortified Roof or IBHS FORTIFIED designation experience (for extra wind resistance and possible insurance discounts).
- Roof certification and wind‑mitigation inspection after installation.
- Lien releases and final inspection documentation.

Questions to ask any contractor
- Are you licensed in Florida and registered with Miami‑Dade County? Can you provide license numbers?
- Have you done hurricane-rated roof replacements in my neighborhood? Any photos or references?
- Which manufacturer warranties will apply, and do you offer a workmanship warranty? How long?
- Will you pull permits and coordinate inspections? Who will handle cleanup?
- What products and attachment details will you use to meet HVHZ/NOA requirements?
- What is your payment schedule? (Avoid large upfront cash demands; common is 10–30% down.)
- Can you provide proof of insurance and bonds?

Red flags
- Door-knockers promising immediate storm-related discounts or asking for full payment up front.
- No written estimate, no permits, or pressure to pay cash.
- Extremely low bids without itemized scope — likely cutting corners or using non-approved materials.
- No local references or inability to produce license/insurance.

If you want, I can:
- Search and shortlist 3–5 highly rated, hurricane-experienced roofers in your Miami zip code.
- Compare their licenses, certifications, example projects, and typical warranties.
Tell me your zip code or address (or whether your roof is flat/low-slope vs. pitched, and what material you prefer) and I’ll pull a vetted short list.
